title: Design System Foundation
outcome: NoorPath has one enforced visual and interaction foundation for customer, operator and administrator surfaces, grounded in the approved Landing and Package references and implemented through reusable tokens, icons, components, layouts and validation rules.
actor: NoorPath customers, approved operators, administrators, agents in future scope, product designers and engineers.
modules: Web owns reusable customer and staff layout primitives, component contracts and rendered examples.
Shared design tokens own semantic colour, typography, spacing, radius, elevation, motion and z-index values.
Design governance owns fixed terminology, icon mapping, package-detail section order and visual-source authority.
Existing domain modules remain unchanged unless a minimal presentation adapter is required to consume shared components.
routes: Customer public shell -> canonical header -> content -> canonical footer
Package details -> repository-approved visual structure -> shared package components
Authorized staff -> shared portal shell -> role-scoped navigation
Design-system showcase/test route -> tokens, icons, states and responsive component examples
acceptance: The approved Landing and Package references remain the visual source of truth and are not redesigned.
Customer and staff surfaces use separate canonical shells while sharing NoorPath brand tokens.
Semantic design tokens replace avoidable raw colours, spacing, radius, elevation, motion and layering values in changed foundation code.
One approved SVG icon system and a fixed NoorPath icon mapping are documented and usable without emoji icons.
Reusable components cover buttons, fields, cards, status badges, support actions, occupancy avatars, feature tiles, timeline states, loading, empty, error and retry states.
The Package Details section order is documented and represented by reusable layout contracts that operators cannot reorder.
Customer and staff headers and footers have explicit responsive and accessibility behaviour.
Interactive controls meet WCAG 2.2 AA, keyboard, focus, target-size, reflow, text-scaling and reduced-motion requirements.
Changed components have rendered desktop and mobile evidence and do not introduce visual drift from approved references.
Existing product behaviour, routes, authorization, financial rules and domain state machines remain unchanged.
Documentation distinguishes current repository truth from historical baseline notes.
The Product Owner approves the exact implementation before merge; deployment remains separately approved.
policyDecisionsRequired: Confirm final customer pre-login and post-login header items.
Confirm final staff sidebar grouping for Overview, Content, Operations and Administration.
Confirm whether the design-system showcase is development-only or available to authorized staff in non-production environments.
Confirm any unresolved typography values only through approved reference comparison, not generic recommendations.
exclusions: Redesigning the approved Landing or Package Details pages.
Implementing the new customer reservation flow, phone OTP changes, package builder business logic, payment options or My Journey feature changes.
Changing operator permissions, administrator approval rules, package publication rules or departure operations.
Adding dark mode, a second icon library, decorative motion or a generic marketplace visual style.
Replacing existing domain APIs, state machines or persistence models.
